images.title: Two rulers, first match
images.purpose: Recap the two ruler method: the first mark after 0 that both rulers share is the LCM, shown for strips of 4 and 10.
images.composition: Two horizontal rulers stacked one above the other in the centre, aligned at 0, with the first shared mark circled; wide margins all round.
exact_structure: Upper ruler, teal #0072B2, name Strips of 4 at its left: exactly 11 tick marks at 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40.
Lower ruler, amber #E69F00, name Strips of 10 at its left: exactly 5 tick marks at 0, 10, 20, 30, 40.
Both rulers are drawn to the same scale and start at the same 0 directly above one another; they end at 40.
Only these ticks carry a number: a single 0, 20 and 40, each written once in the gap between the two rulers; every other tick has no number.
The ticks at 20 on both rulers are joined by one vertical reddish purple #CC79A7 line inside a reddish purple circle, with the text LCM = 20 just below the lower ruler at that point.
The ticks at 40 on both rulers are joined by one thin grey #6B7280 vertical line with no circle.
No mark at 0 is circled or highlighted.
rejection: 0 marked or circled as the LCM
other than exactly 11 ticks on the upper ruler and 5 ticks on the lower ruler
any extra numbers on the ticks, or the circle at any place other than 20
any of the numbers 6, 8 or 24 appearing
images.takeaway: The first length after 0 that both rulers show is the LCM, and the matches keep going after it.
images.description: Two aligned rulers, one with marks every 4 and one with marks every 10, meet first at 20, circled as LCM = 20, and again at 40.
images.context: Shown beside the toran builder practice tool.
images.teaching_notes: Slide along both rulers from 0 and stop at the first shared mark; that is the shortest equal toran.

image_decisions.why: A two ruler recap mirrors the practice tool and shows the first match as the LCM.
